## Website

[↑ Contents](#contents)

- [**Power BI API Scraper: decoding a published report query format**](https://github.com/artemiyDev/powerbi_api_scraper) - Power BI API Scraper reconstructs the web client's undocumented query and response format for published reports. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · Also: Protocol · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/power-bi-report-query-case/)</sub>
- [**Sheypoor MCP: mapping marketplace APIs from browser traffic**](https://github.com/FarhamAghdasi/sheypoor-mcp) - Sheypoor MCP implements a client and MCP server for the Sheypoor classifieds site using API behavior documented from browser traffic. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/sheypoor-mcp-case/)</sub>
- [**ZCode-Android: reconstructing the ZCode remote-control client**](https://github.com/Damianjiang/ZCode-Android) - ZCode-Android recreates ZCode remote control on Android from captured traffic and analysis of its official web page. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · Also: App, Protocol · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/zcode-android-case/)</sub>
- [**Terminal: a Rust terminal informed by TradingView chart research**](https://github.com/michaelshimeles/terminal) - An independent Rust market interface uses REA browser-scenario research on public logged-out TradingView chart interactions. <sub>Case study · Mixed workflow · Also: App · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/terminal-tradingview-rea-chart-case/)</sub>
- [**Littlebird.ai static home-page rebuild**](https://github.com/AkashNaickar/crdb-sample-frontend) - Rebuilds the Littlebird.ai home page in plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript from captured markup and assets, with source-wired mobile navigation, FAQ toggles, scroll reveals and OS-dependent call-to-action presentation. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/littlebird-static-rebuild-case/)</sub>
- [**Ruffle: a Rust reimplementation of Adobe Flash Player**](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle) - Reimplements Adobe Flash Player in Rust so that SWF content, from ActionScript 1/2 (AVM1) to ActionScript 3 (AVM2), runs in a native desktop player or in browsers through WebAssembly, as a self-hosted script or a browser extension. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · Also: Game · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/ruffle-flash-player-case/)</sub>
- [**Dinosaur runner: an REA-inspected speed rule rebuilt with Codex**](https://github.com/zhxunzh84/rea-dino-reverse-engineering) - The author uses REA’s MCP browser tools to passively capture the JavaScript loaded by wayou’s open-source T-Rex Runner page, then has Codex rebuild its acceleration rule in one self-contained HTML5 Canvas game. <sub>Case study · Mixed workflow · Also: Game · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/rea-dino-runner-community-case/)</sub>
- [**whatsapp-web-reveng: documenting the legacy WhatsApp Web protocol**](https://github.com/sigalor/whatsapp-web-reveng) - Documents and reimplements the WebSocket protocol WhatsApp Web used while browser sessions mirrored a paired phone: QR pairing, Curve25519/HKDF key setup, AES/HMAC-protected binary messages, the token-based node encoding and end-to-end media encryption. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · Also: Protocol · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/whatsapp-web-reveng-legacy-protocol-case/)</sub>
- [**BaoCut Design: porting reconstructed canvas and design-system editors**](https://github.com/JimLiu/baocut/tree/7aa049e82e1367da013b7aba80f0b79033fa04ad/packages/design-runtime) - Documents BaoCut’s design-canvas and design-system editors, which the project says it ported 1:1 from TypeScript reconstructions of Claude Design’s editors and hosts in agent sessions with annotation and export. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · Also: App · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/baocut-design-canvas-case/)</sub>
- [**REA in Claude Code: an isolated static-analysis A/B trial**](https://zenn.dev/keigoly/articles/8738d8d241b5a1) - A Japanese field report connects REA 6.4.0 to Claude Code in a separate project directory, denies 43 of its 170 tools and common shell launch forms, and compares REA-enabled and REA-disabled runs on two real tasks: an Electron terminal’s packaged files and a saved HAR capture. <sub>Case study · Mixed workflow · Also: App · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/rea-claude-code-isolated-ab-case/)</sub>
- [**BaoCut Slides: adapting an interactive web editor**](https://github.com/JimLiu/baocut/tree/b8585e0c8d7a82bdee9f0ed019cf6edb075e41c1/packages/slides-runtime) - Documents BaoCut’s interactive slide editor, whose author says the implementation draws on Claude Slides. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · Also: App · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/baocut-slides-editor-case/)</sub>
- [**Dinosaur runner: recovering one acceleration rule**](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/c360cfcd6d7901514b16dd6113eba2e0b0fdf422/website/evidence/calculator-and-dino.md#dinosaur-speed) - REA’s documented teaching case inspects the HTTP t-rex-runner edition and reconstructs its speed-update rule. <sub>Case study · Official REA · Also: Game · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/rea-dinosaur-speed-case/)</sub>
- [**rauchg.com: rebuilding an RSC blog from captured Flight output**](https://github.com/boyang-hu/website-rebuild-skill/blob/ac60c9d8a2ab40045a89b5403c3457f1404e92b3/skills/website-rebuild/references/rsc-reconstruction.md) - Documents a website-rebuild-skill case that decodes browser-delivered React Server Component Flight streams, reconstructs a buildable Next project and compares its output with a captured site. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/rauchg-rsc-reconstruction-case/)</sub>

### Matching decompilations and disassemblies (69)

- [**3S Decomp: a byte-compared PS2 decompilation of Street Fighter III: 3rd Strike**](https://github.com/crowded-street/3s-decomp) - Decompiles the PlayStation 2 executable of Street Fighter III: 3rd Strike from Street Fighter Anniversary Collection into C that period Metrowerks and EE GCC compilers rebuild, then compares the rebuilt executable word by word with the user’s original. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/sfiii-3rd-strike-ps2-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Agent decompilation: a byte-matching retrospective**](https://momo5502.com/posts/2026-10-09-game-decompilation/) - Maurice Heumann describes replacing plausible-looking agent output with compiler-based checks of reconstructed functions, relocations, data and types. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/agent-decompilation-oracle-case/)</sub>
- [**Animal Crossing: matching GameCube decompilation**](https://github.com/ACreTeam/ac-decomp) - Reconstructs Animal Crossing’s GameCube code as C and C++ source that rebuilds the USA release’s main executable and its foresta.rel module. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/animal-crossing-gamecube-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Animal Crossing: Wild World: matching Korean DS decompilation with differential runtime checks**](https://github.com/banatic/acww-decomp) - Reconstructs the ARM9 game code of Animal Crossing: Wild World’s Korean DS release as one C or C++ source per function, checked against the user’s ROM with the original Metrowerks compiler and linker. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/animal-crossing-wild-world-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Animal Forest: an in-progress matching N64 decompilation**](https://github.com/zeldaret/af) - Rebuilds the Japanese Nintendo 64 release of Animal Forest (Dōbutsu no Mori) from C code reverse-engineered from the ROM, combined with assets and assembly extracted from a user-supplied ROM. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/animal-forest-n64-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**BFM-decomp: Brave Fencer Musashi matching decompilation**](https://github.com/Druthulu/BFM-decomp) - Documents an agent-assisted reconstruction of the USA PlayStation game with a pinned compiler and whole-binary SHA-1 gates. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · Also: Binary · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/bfm-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Breath of the Wild: per-function matching decompilation of the Switch executable**](https://github.com/zeldaret/botw) - Reimplements part of Breath of the Wild’s Switch v1.5.0 main executable in C++ and checks each function against the original machine code. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/botw-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Castlevania: Symphony of the Night: matching decompilation across PlayStation, PSP and Saturn builds**](https://github.com/Xeeynamo/sotn-decomp) - Recreates C source for Castlevania: Symphony of the Night from its PlayStation, PSP and Saturn binaries, aiming for code that compiles byte for byte to the original game files. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/sotn-matching-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**DX-Ball: an REA-guided function-level reconstruction with Codex**](https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/dx-ball) - The author has Codex use REA’s Ghidra tools to inspect the English DX-Ball 1.07 executable and recover it as typed C/C++, then compiles each function with the original-era Visual C++ 4.0 and compares it byte for byte with the original after mapping relocations. <sub>Case study · Mixed workflow · Also: Binary · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/dx-ball-rea-reconstruction-case/)</sub>
- [**DX-Ball: reconstruct sound panning**](https://rea.tools/showcase/dx-ball/) - Recover one sound-pan function from instructions and constants; upstream cites 3,205 cases and a 63-byte match. <sub>Case study · Official REA · Also: Binary · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/rea-dxball-case/)</sub>
- [**Final Fantasy VII: a matching PlayStation decompilation**](https://github.com/Xeeynamo/ff7-decomp) - Reconstructs C source for the US PlayStation release of Final Fantasy VII, aiming for code that compiles back to the original main executable and its game overlays. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/ff7-ps1-matching-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**GoldenEye 007: matching Nintendo 64 decompilation for three releases**](https://github.com/n64decomp/007) - Reconstructs GoldenEye 007’s Nintendo 64 code as C source that rebuilds the US, Japanese and PAL ROMs. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/goldeneye-007-matching-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Gran Turismo 4: an agent-assisted PS2 engine matching decompilation**](https://github.com/gustavocanepa/gt4-decomp) - Decompiles Gran Turismo 4’s PS2 engine executable (CORE.GT4, NTSC-U v1.01) into one C or C++ source per function for Sony’s ee-gcc 2.96, matching public libraries such as newlib and Expat from their own source. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/gran-turismo-4-matching-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Halo 2: an agent-assisted matching decompilation of an LTCG Xbox build**](https://github.com/kirklandsig/halo2-decompiled) - A work-in-progress matching decompilation of Halo 2 for the original Xbox: contributors write C and C++ that the period compiler, building the whole program with link-time code generation, must turn back into the retail executable's bytes function by function. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/halo2-matching-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Himuro: a matching Fatal Frame PS2 decompilation**](https://github.com/Mikompilation/Himuro) - Reconstructs Fatal Frame’s PS2 executable as C for the US, EU and Japanese releases, built with the original EE-GCC 2.9 toolchain and checked by SHA-1 against the user’s own executables. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/himuro-fatal-frame-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**ICO decompilation: byte-identical PAL and Japanese PlayStation 2 boot ELFs**](https://github.com/nathanialf/ico) - Rebuilds the boot ELFs of ICO’s PAL (SCES-50760) and Japanese (SCPS-11003) PlayStation 2 discs from one source tree with the game’s original compiler versions, and checks that every loaded byte and the whole ELF file match the disc’s SHA-1. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/ico-matching-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days: a matching Nintendo DS decompilation**](https://github.com/Yokimitsuro/khdays-decomp) - Reconstructs the ARM9 program and overlays of the EU Nintendo DS release of Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days as C that recompiles byte for byte with CodeWarrior. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/kingdom-hearts-days-matching-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**LEGO Island: source reconstruction with separately reported exact rebuilds**](https://github.com/isledecomp/isle) - Reconstructs the English LEGO Island 1.1 source for its original 32-bit Windows target. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/lego-island-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Majora’s Mask: matching US N64 decompilation**](https://github.com/zeldaret/mm) - Recreates a C source base for The Legend of Zelda: Majora’s Mask from information in the game and static or dynamic analysis, then rebuilds the US Nintendo 64 ROM. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/zelda-mm-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Mario Kart Wii: an in-progress matching decompilation of the PAL release**](https://github.com/snailspeed3/mkw) - A work-in-progress matching decompilation of Mario Kart Wii that targets the PAL release (RMCP01), rebuilding main.dol and the StaticR.rel module from C and C++ with Metrowerks compilers and checking both against stored SHA-1 values. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/mario-kart-wii-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Mario Kart: Double Dash!!: a matching GameCube decompilation of the debug build**](https://github.com/doldecomp/mkdd) - A work-in-progress 1:1 decompilation of Mario Kart: Double Dash!! <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/mario-kart-double-dash-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Mario Party 4: matching GameCube decompilation of the USA releases**](https://github.com/mariopartyrd/marioparty4) - Reconstructs Mario Party 4’s GameCube main executable and REL modules as C source that rebuilds both USA releases. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/mario-party-4-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**MediEvil decompilation: an early checksum-gated PlayStation project**](https://github.com/MediEvilDecompilation/medievil-decomp) - Decompiles the US PlayStation release of MediEvil toward C source that rebuilds its main executable, game executable and 26 overlays. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/medievil-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Metroid Prime: the PrimeDecomp matching GameCube decompilation**](https://github.com/PrimeDecomp/prime) - Reconstructs C++ source for Metroid Prime’s GameCube executable and its NES-emulator module so that CodeWarrior builds match the originals, across the USA, Korean, PAL and Japanese releases, with early configurations for demo discs and three Wii releases. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/primedecomp-metroid-prime-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**MinecraftLCE: an early-stage Minecraft: Nintendo Switch Edition decompilation**](https://github.com/GRAnimated/MinecraftLCE) - Decompiles Minecraft: Nintendo Switch Edition v1.0.17, a Legacy Console Edition release, into C++ that is compared function by function with the original executable using a patched Clang 4.0.1 and the open-ead Switch decompilation tools. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/minecraft-lce-switch-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Ocarina of Time: decompilation with MD5-checked ROM builds for 16 versions**](https://github.com/zeldaret/oot) - Recreates a C source base for Ocarina of Time that rebuilds 16 Nintendo 64, GameCube and iQue Player ROM versions, using information from the game and static and dynamic analysis. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/ocarina-of-time-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Paper Mario: matching Nintendo 64 decompilation for four releases**](https://github.com/pmret/papermario) - Reconstructs Paper Mario’s Nintendo 64 code as C source that rebuilds the US, Japanese, PAL and iQue ROMs. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/paper-mario-matching-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door: an early matching GameCube decompilation**](https://github.com/doldecomp/ttyd) - A work-in-progress matching decompilation of Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door that targets the Japanese Rev 0 GameCube release (G8MJ01), rebuilding MarioSt.dol and 31 REL modules with the original Metrowerks compilers and checking each against a stored SHA-1. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/paper-mario-ttyd-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Perfect Dark: matching Nintendo 64 decompilation**](https://github.com/n64decomp/perfect_dark) - Reconstructs Perfect Dark’s Nintendo 64 code with a documented matching-ROM build. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/perfect-dark-matching-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Petari: a matching Super Mario Galaxy decompilation**](https://github.com/SMGCommunity/Petari) - Reconstructs Super Mario Galaxy’s Wii code as C++ that rebuilds, object by object, against main.dol files extracted from the user’s own Japanese, North American, PAL or Korean disc. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/petari-smg-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Phantom Hourglass: an early-stage matching Nintendo DS decompilation**](https://github.com/zeldaret/ph) - Recreates C++ source for The Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass by hand-decompiling its European and US Nintendo DS releases, using the dsd toolkit to delink code from a user-supplied ROM and rebuild the ROM. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/phantom-hourglass-ds-decomp-case/)</sub>

- [**pokecrystal: a matching Pokémon Crystal disassembly**](https://github.com/pret/pokecrystal) - Reconstructs the Game Boy Color game Pokémon Crystal as RGBDS assembly, with graphics, maps and data stored as editable sources. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/pokecrystal-disassembly-case/)</sub>
- [**pokered: a matching Pokémon Red and Blue disassembly**](https://github.com/pret/pokered) - Reconstructs the Game Boy games Pokémon Red and Blue as RGBDS assembly, with graphics and data kept as editable source files. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/pokered-disassembly-case/)</sub>

- [**Pokémon Emerald: a matching Game Boy Advance decompilation**](https://github.com/pret/pokeemerald) - Reconstructs Pokémon Emerald for the Game Boy Advance as buildable C source, with game scripts and data kept as assembler directives. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/pokemon-emerald-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Pokémon FireRed and LeafGreen: a matching Game Boy Advance decompilation**](https://github.com/pret/pokefirered) - Reconstructs the English Game Boy Advance releases of Pokémon FireRed and LeafGreen as buildable C source, with game scripts and data kept as assembler directives. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/pokemon-firered-leafgreen-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver: a work-in-progress, checksum-matched DS disassembly**](https://github.com/pret/pokeheartgold) - Rebuilds the US Nintendo DS releases of Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver from a work-in-progress disassembly in which part of the code has been decompiled to C. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/pokemon-heartgold-soulsilver-disassembly-case/)</sub>
- [**Pokémon Platinum: a checksum-matched Nintendo DS decompilation**](https://github.com/pret/pokeplatinum) - Reconstructs the US Nintendo DS release of Pokémon Platinum as C source that rebuilds revision 1 by default and revision 0 on request. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/pokemon-platinum-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**pw: a matching decompilation of the Pokéwalker firmware**](https://github.com/lumirth/pw) - Reconstructs as C the firmware of the Pokéwalker, the pedometer accessory for Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver, for its Renesas H8/38606 microcontroller. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · Also: Firmware · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/pokewalker-matching-decomp-case/)</sub>
- [**Ratchet &amp; Clank: a matching PS2 decompilation with a documented agent workflow**](https://github.com/OpenRAC/rac1-decomp) - Reconstructs C source for SCES\_509.16, the PAL v2.00 PlayStation 2 executable of Ratchet &amp; Clank (2002), with every function linked at its retail address. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/rac1-matching-decomp-case/)</sub>

- [**Snowboard Kids: an agent-assisted N64 matching decompilation**](https://github.com/cdlewis/snowboardkids-decomp) - A matching decompilation of the original Nintendo 64 Snowboard Kids that rebuilds SHA1-identical North American and Japanese ROMs from a user-supplied ROM. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/snowboardkids-matching-decomp-case/)</sub>

- [**OpenDMCUFirm: a reimplemented Wii U DMCU display firmware**](https://github.com/GaryOderNichts/OpenDMCUFirm) - Reimplements in C the firmware of the Wii U’s DMCU, the M68HC11-compatible display microcontroller in its AMD graphics controller, which in Wii mode reads the Video Interface state and configures display output, deinterlacing, scaling and overscan. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/opendmcufirm-wii-u-dmcu-firmware-case/)</sub>
- [**reflecticon-224: running Lexicon 224 reverb firmware on emulated hardware**](https://github.com/joelanders/reflecticon-224) - Emulates the Lexicon 224, 224X and 224XL digital reverbs so that their own firmware runs in a browser page or a JUCE plugin. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/reflecticon-224-lexicon-emulation-case/)</sub>
- [**Supermodel: initial Real3D Pro-1000 image-generator emulation**](https://github.com/trzy/Supermodel) - Adds emulation of Real3D’s Pro-1000, the SCSI-attached image generator from which Sega’s Model 3 graphics hardware derives, to the Supermodel arcade emulator. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/supermodel-real3d-pro1000-emulation-case/)</sub>
- [**flipper-telink: replacement firmware for Tuya Zigbee remotes**](https://github.com/ngxson/flipper-telink) - A Flipper Zero app that bit-bangs Telink’s SWire debug interface to dump and reflash TLSR825x Zigbee devices, with static-analysis notes on the dumps and freshly written firmware for two of them. <sub>Case study · Independent reconstruction · [Full entry](https://awesomerea.org/resources/flipper-telink-tuya-remote-firmware-case/)</sub>
